messages:
lee: Heads up: we need a short-lived SIEM export for vuln triage on host prod-db-03. It's got unusual egress. Filing ticket TKT-4821 to request a scrubbed export + decrypt window.

nandini: OK. Follow the JIT-unlock runbook. Basics: exports must be field-sanitized, written encrypted to our audit S3, and only unwrapped via the kms-proxy after dual approver OK. Default unwrap TTL = 48h, export TTL = 7d.

lee: Dual approver = two named approvers or two roles?

nandini: Two named people with appropriate entitlements: at least one security lead plus either oncall IC or infra owner. Both must sign in the ticket.

kai: Question: can the exporter service call KMS:Decrypt directly for the unwrap? We try to avoid broad Decrypt perms.

oscar: Don't give exporter direct Decrypt. Pattern: exporter encrypts with exporter-wrapping-key and writes object. When approved, kms-proxy (tiny service) performs one-time unwrap and streams to an ephemeral analysis VM. Proxy logs requester, ticket id, approvers, and expiry.

sec-bot: TKT-4821 created by lee. Add approvers and desired decrypt window. See https://internal.runbooks/redwood/security/jit-unlock for guidance.

lee: What fields do we need in the export? Full events or redacted?

nandini: Keep core forensic fields only: timestamp, host, process, src_ip, dst_ip, port, event_type, exit_code. Remove or pseudonymize user identifiers. If analyst needs a stable mapping, use HMAC pseudonymization keyed to the ticket vault. No raw emails, SSNs, auth tokens.

kai: Example scrub rules (informal):

```
keep: ["timestamp","host","process","src_ip","dst_ip","port","event_type"]
drop: ["user_email","auth_token","ssn"]
pseudonymize: {"user_id": "hmac-sha256:VAULT_KEY_ID"}
output_prefix: "s3://redwood-audit/exports/TKT-4821/"
```

oscar: Also require object metadata tags: ticket_id, approvers, unwrap_expiry_ts, scrub_version, justification_summary. These help auditors find the context quickly.

lee: For high-sensitivity items can we set unwrap TTL to 24h?

nandini: Yes — default is 48h but 24h is encouraged for PII risk. Anything >48h requires CISO signoff and a documented business justification.

lee: Analysts often like to download to local machine. Allowed?

oscar: Not allowed. All analysis must happen in approved ephemeral VMs with disk encryption and blocked outbound. If artifacts need to leave the VM, run the scrub-review flow and record it in the ticket.

kai: Will the proxy enforce the 1-time unwrap and delete the plaintext on completion?

oscar: Yes. Proxy grants a short-lived access token scoped to the VM session, records the unwrap event, and triggers a post-export validator that confirms no prohibited fields remain.

lee: I'm adding approvers now: @nandini and @kai. Requesting 48h unwrap, bastion analysis, and HMAC pseudonyms. Ticket updated.

sec-bot: Approver kai approved TKT-4821 at 3748003410. Audit entry logged.

kai: Approved. I confirm exporter will run field-filtering before upload and will not have KMS:Decrypt. oscar: please wire the proxy.

oscar: Will do. Proxy will tag unwrap with ticket=TKT-4821 and expiry=3748171810 (48h). It will also emit an audit event to splunk and create a KMS-unlock record.

nandini: Action items: lee 92 confirm host list and extraction query (pending). kai 92 verify exporter scrub config. oscar 92 configure proxy unwrap + run post-export checks. Security will sample validate the scrubbed output.

lee: Done, query and host list added to the ticket. Closing loop after triage.

nandini: Post-action: if scrubber flagged ambiguous PII matches, open an eval task to improve ruleset. :mag:
